determinism: Rows, families, and output keys use stable ordering; the model uses one thread and a fixed seed; runtime timestamps are intentionally omitted.

human_split_summary.method: stable seeded hash split of opaque participant groups

limitations: This is a retrospective family holdout inside one public corpus, not a prospective test on future agents or new collection environments.
Agent family is confounded with its software, browser/OS setup, model, and collection period; browser-fingerprint results can exploit those environment differences rather than interaction style.
The corpus contains three website tasks. This protocol holds out an agent family, not a task; task transfer is not established.
The fixed human test set is reused across seven family folds. Macro summaries average family-level point estimates and are descriptive, not seven independent estimates of human performance.
Rows are repeated task attempts, not an independently sampled population. No population-level deployment claim or uncertainty interval is made.

protocol_details.agent_split: leave one named agent family out in each fold
protocol_details.duplicate_handling: collapse exact duplicate 468-dimensional combined vectors within each family before every feature-set evaluation
protocol_details.human_split: one fixed 80/20-style split by opaque participant group; the same human test set is reused only to make family folds comparable
protocol_details.model: binary XGBoost classifier trained from scratch per fold
protocol_details.training_balance: inverse-frequency sample weights; mean weight is 1

question: Can a binary classifier trained on Human plus six known agent families identify the seventh, unseen family as agent-generated?
